_: Turkish voice-assistant TTS test set: 189 everyday sentences an assistant actually says, in 15 categories. Distribution and patterns follow 1,157 assistant sentences from 111 real calls (median 7 words; 38% questions, 21% brand names, 9% digits, 5% abbreviations); hard categories are deliberately over-represented. Fully synthetic: no real person, company or phone number. Categories were also drawn from other test sets: Freya-TR-Eval (plain everyday sentences, questions, exclamations), Gradium's hard-case set (abbreviations, alphanumerics, dates, numbers, e-mail and combined replies) and EmergentTTS-Eval (foreign words, questions, tone). text = what is sent to the TTS model (as an LLM writes it, with digits). spoken = the same sentence as it is read; it is both a second input (the model's own number reading is bypassed) and the scoring reference; when absent it equals text. alt = other accepted readings. entities = critical information scored separately (name: whole words, phone: digits, email: written form); a sentence is fully correct only if every entity is heard correctly.
